name: Salesforce (REST/SOAP APIs via External Client App)
verdict: Build a Packaged External Client App (not a Connected App) in a free Developer Edition org, ship it in a 2GP managed package, and have each customer's admin install it; plan for per-org admin friction, not a central Salesforce review.

difficulty.label: Moderate
difficulty.rationale: No mandatory Salesforce review for OAuth, and a dev token takes under an hour. But since Spring '26 new Connected Apps are disabled by default, a Local External Client App only serves its own org, and since Sept 2025 uninstalled apps are blocked for most users. So multi-org production means 2GP packaging plus an admin install in every customer org. AppExchange security review is optional (roughly 3–9 weeks per attempt depending on queue).

first_token.note: Sign up for a Developer Edition org, create a Local External Client App, then wait up to ~10 min for it to become active before the first authorize call.

production.estimate: 1–2 weeks to a shippable package; then days–weeks per customer org; +4–8 weeks if you list on AppExchange
production.active_effort: 1–3 days (Dev Hub, namespace, 2GP package, install docs for admins)
production.waiting: Mostly each customer admin's change-control process to install the package and assign access; optional AppExchange security review ~3–9 weeks per lap
production.note: Salesforce does not centrally approve OAuth clients. What gates production is (a) packaging the ECA so it can be installed cross-org, (b) customer admins installing it and granting Permitted Users/permission sets, and (c) customers being on an edition with API access.

cost: Free (Developer Edition org, ECA, 2GP packaging). Optional AppExchange security review: $999 per attempt for paid solutions (official, since March 2023; waived for free solutions). Customers need Enterprise/Performance/Unlimited/Developer edition, or Professional + paid API add-on.

paths.name: Local External Client App (single org)
paths.who_for: Your own org, internal tools, a single customer whose admin creates the ECA in their own org and gives you the keys.
paths.limits: Only users of the org that created it can authorize; other orgs get 'Cross-org OAuth flows are not supported for this external client app'.

paths.name: Packaged External Client App via 2GP managed package (multi-tenant)
paths.who_for: SaaS / AI-agent products connecting many customer orgs with one consumer key.
paths.review: No Salesforce review needed to share an install link; each customer admin must install and approve.
paths.limits: Needs Dev Hub + registered namespace (two separate DE orgs). Customer admin controls Permitted Users, refresh token policy, IP relaxation, session timeout.

paths.name: AppExchange listing
paths.who_for: Vendors wanting discoverability and the trust signal; enterprise customers often require it.
paths.review: AppExchange security review (static scan, dynamic test, manual review).
paths.limits: Typically 3–9 weeks per submission; resubmissions re-queue; fee for paid solutions.

prerequisites.item: Salesforce Developer Edition org (free) at developer.salesforce.com/signup
prerequisites.note: Needs a unique username in email format and email verification. Use a second DE org for the namespace if you will package.

prerequisites.item: User permission 'Create, edit, and delete External Client Apps' (System Administrator has it in DE)
prerequisites.note: Needed to see New External Client App.

prerequisites.item: HTTPS callback URL on your backend (e.g. https://app.example.com/oauth/salesforce/callback)
prerequisites.note: Exact match against Callback URL field.
sf --version; used for Dev Hub login, package create/version/promote.

prerequisites.item: Customer orgs on Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited or Developer edition (or Professional + API add-on), users with 'API Enabled'
prerequisites.note: Confirm during sales/onboarding; otherwise calls fail with API_DISABLED_FOR_ORG.

steps.title: Create a Developer Edition org
steps.detail: Sign up at developer.salesforce.com/signup, verify email, set password. Note your My Domain URL (https://<name>.develop.my.salesforce.com). If you will distribute, create a second DE org now for namespace registration.

steps.title: Create an External Client App (not a Connected App)
steps.detail: Setup > Quick Find 'App Manager' (or 'External Client App Manager') > New External Client App. Basic Information: External Client App Name, API Name, Contact Email, Distribution State = Local (for dev) or Packaged (for distribution; do this in the Dev Hub org). Do not try 'New Connected App' — creation is disabled by default since Spring '26 and needs a Support case.

steps.title: Enable OAuth and select scopes
steps.detail: Expand API (Enable OAuth Settings) > check Enable OAuth. Callback URL: your exact HTTPS callback (one per line). Selected OAuth Scopes: 'Manage user data via APIs (api)', 'Perform requests at any time (refresh_token, offline_access)', 'Access unique user identifiers (openid)'. Flow Enablement: Enable Authorization Code and Credentials Flow. Security: keep 'Require Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)', 'Require Secret for Web Server Flow', 'Require Secret for Refresh Token Flow' unless you have a reason. Create.

steps.title: Copy Consumer Key and Secret
steps.detail: Open the app > Settings tab > OAuth Settings > Consumer Key and Secret. Salesforce emails a verification code before revealing them. Store in your secret manager (consumer key = client_id, consumer secret = client_secret).

steps.title: Set OAuth policies in your org
steps.detail: App > Policies tab > Edit. OAuth Policies: Permitted Users (All users may self-authorize vs Admin approved users are pre-authorized), Refresh Token Policy = 'Refresh token is valid until revoked' for agents, IP Relaxation. Note: in customer orgs their admin sets these, not you.

steps.title: Wait for propagation, then run the web server flow with PKCE
steps.detail: Wait up to ~10 minutes after creating/editing. Redirect user to https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&scope=api%20refresh_token%20openid&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256&state=... Exchange at /services/oauth2/token with code_verifier + client_secret. Persist instance_url and id from the response; call APIs at {instance_url}/services/data/vXX.X/.

steps.title: Set up Dev Hub and namespace for packaging
steps.detail: Org A: Setup > Dev Hub > Enable Dev Hub (irreversible). Org B: Setup > Package Manager > Register Namespace. In Org A App Launcher > Namespace Registries > Link Namespace and log into Org B. A single org cannot be both Dev Hub and namespace org.

steps.title: Create a Packaged ECA and 2GP managed package
steps.detail: In the Dev Hub create the ECA with Distribution State = Packaged (same OAuth config). Then: sf org login web --set-default-dev-hub; sf project generate; sf package create --package-type Managed --path force-app; retrieve ExternalClientApplication, ExtlClntAppOauthSettings (and ExtlClntAppOauthConfigurablePolicies) via package.xml; set namespace in sfdx-project.json; sf package version create --installation-key-bypass --code-coverage --wait 20. Global OAuth settings (consumer secret) are not packaged.

steps.title: Promote the package version and publish install instructions
steps.detail: Promote the version (sf package version promote) so it installs in production orgs (beta versions install only in sandboxes/scratch/DE). Write an admin guide: install URL, 'Install for Admins Only' vs specific profiles, then Setup > External Client App Manager > your app > Policies: Permitted Users, assign permission set/profile, Refresh Token Policy 'valid until revoked'.

steps.title: Customer admin installs and grants access
steps.detail: Each customer admin opens the install link (login.salesforce.com for prod, test.salesforce.com for sandbox), installs, then grants users access. Only then can their users complete your OAuth flow.

steps.title: Optional: AppExchange security review
steps.detail: Partner Community > Publishing Console > create listing > submit for security review with scanner reports (Code Analyzer), test org credentials, and docs for your external endpoints.

review.trigger: Only if you list on AppExchange. No review is required to create an ECA or to distribute a managed package by install link; instead every customer org's admin must install/approve the app.
review.process: AppExchange: submit package + listing in the Partner Console; Salesforce Product Security runs static analysis, dynamic testing and manual review including your external web app/API endpoints.
review.typical_wait: ~3–9 weeks per submission (ISVforce guide: ~3–4 weeks to initial report; Salesforce's 2023 blog cited a 6–9 week queue); failures add another full lap.
reviewers_check: Secure storage of OAuth tokens and secrets on your servers
common_rejections: Reviewer cannot log into the test org

pre_approval_limits: Local ECA works only for users in the org where it was created (cross-org flows rejected).
Uninstalled apps: since Sept 2025 only users with 'Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps' (or 'Use Any API Client' when API Access Control is on) can authorize an app not installed in their org.
Developer Edition: 5 MB data storage and low API daily limits; fine for testing only.
Beta (unpromoted) 2GP versions cannot be installed in customer production orgs.

oauth.authorize_url: https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/authorize (sandbox: https://test.salesforce.com/...; or the org's My Domain https://<domain>.my.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/authorize)
oauth.refresh_tokens: Issued when refresh_token (offline_access) scope is granted. Lifetime is governed by the Refresh Token Policy set by the admin of each org (valid until revoked [default], expire after X, expire if unused for X, immediately expire). Optional refresh token rotation setting on the ECA.
oauth.access_token_lifetime: Not a fixed TTL: tied to the org's session timeout (commonly 2 h; admins can change per org/profile). Treat 401 INVALID_SESSION_ID as 'refresh now'.
oauth.redirect_uri_rules: Must match a Callback URL registered on the app exactly; HTTPS required for web apps (http://localhost is accepted for local dev in practice). Multiple callback URLs allowed, one per line.
oauth.scopes: Coarse scopes: api, refresh_token/offline_access, openid, id/profile/email, web, full, plus feature scopes (chatter_api, cdp_*, sfap_api, einstein_gpt_api…). Real data access is governed by the user's profile/permission sets (object/field security), not by scope.
oauth.tenant_notes: Every customer org has its own instance_url — always store instance_url from the token response and call APIs there. Production users log in via login.salesforce.com, sandbox users via test.salesforce.com; orgs with enforced My Domain login may require their My Domain host. Ask the user for environment (prod/sandbox/custom domain) before redirecting.

gotchas.title: New Connected Apps are disabled by default — use External Client Apps
gotchas.detail: Since Spring '26 'New Connected App' is disabled by default in all orgs (UI and API); re-enabling requires a Salesforce Support case and Salesforce says even that exception is temporary. Existing Connected Apps keep working. Salesforce's own docs tie the change to Spring '26 (Help: "New connected apps can no longer be created in Spring '26").

gotchas.title: A Local ECA cannot authorize users from other orgs
gotchas.detail: ECAs only connect users in the org that created them unless installed in the target org. Error: 'Cross-org OAuth flows are not supported for this external client app'. For multi-tenant SaaS you must package (2GP managed) and have customers install.

gotchas.title: Uninstalled apps blocked for most users since Sept 2025
gotchas.detail: Users now need 'Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps' (or 'Use Any API Client' if API Access Control is enabled) to authorize an app not installed in their org. Symptom: OAUTH_APPROVAL_ERROR_GENERIC / error=invalid_client&error_description=app+must+be+installed+into+org. Fix: have the admin install the app (Setup > Connected Apps OAuth Usage > Install, or install your package).

gotchas.title: Up to ~10 minutes before a new/edited app works
gotchas.detail: Freshly created apps commonly fail with invalid_client_id / redirect mismatch for several minutes. Wait before debugging.

gotchas.title: Customer edition must include API access
gotchas.detail: Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited and Developer include API access; Professional only via paid add-on. Users also need the 'API Enabled' permission. Qualify customers before onboarding.

gotchas.title: Refresh token lifetime is the customer admin's decision
gotchas.detail: Each org's admin sets the Refresh Token Policy for your installed app; if they choose 'expire if not used for X' or 'immediately expire', your agent will lose access. Document the recommended 'valid until revoked' setting in your install guide.

gotchas.title: PKCE and secret requirements are on by default
gotchas.detail: New ECAs default to Require PKCE + Require Secret for Web Server and Refresh Token flows. Omitting code_challenge gives 'missing required code challenge'; public clients failing refresh usually need 'Require Secret for Refresh Token Flow' turned off.

gotchas.title: Migrating a Connected App to an ECA issues new credentials
gotchas.detail: The migration tool generates a new Consumer Key/Secret; old ones stop working and every existing user must re-authorize. Migration is one-way.

gotchas.title: Packaging needs two DE orgs and is irreversible
gotchas.detail: Enabling Dev Hub is permanent; the namespace must be registered in a different org and linked. ECAs support 2GP only (no 1GP).

blockers.symptom: 'New Connected App' button missing or creation blocked
blockers.cause: Connected App creation disabled by default (Spring '26).
blockers.fix: Create an External Client App instead; only if you truly need a Connected App, open a Salesforce Support case.

blockers.symptom: Cross-org OAuth flows are not supported for this external client app
blockers.cause: ECA is Local or not installed in the user's org.
blockers.fix: Package the ECA (Distribution State = Packaged, 2GP managed) and have the customer admin install it.

blockers.symptom: OAUTH_APPROVAL_ERROR_GENERIC or error_description=app must be installed into org
blockers.fix: Customer admin installs the app/package, or grants 'Approve Uninstalled Connected Apps' to the authorizing user (or 'Use Any API Client' if API Access Control is on).

blockers.symptom: invalid_client_id or redirect_uri_mismatch right after creating the app
blockers.fix: Wait ~10 min; compare redirect_uri byte-for-byte with Callback URL.

blockers.symptom: API_DISABLED_FOR_ORG / API is not enabled for this Organization or Partner
blockers.cause: Customer on Professional/Essentials without API add-on, or user lacks API Enabled.
blockers.fix: Customer buys API add-on/upgrades edition; admin enables 'API Enabled' on the profile/permission set.

blockers.cause: Org's Refresh Token Policy expired the token, user revoked, or admin changed policy.
blockers.fix: Ask the admin to set 'Refresh token is valid until revoked'; prompt user to reconnect.

blockers.symptom: invalid_grant: authentication failure on sandbox user
blockers.fix: Use test.salesforce.com or the org's My Domain for sandbox.

agent_can: Generate ECA metadata (ExternalClientApplication, ExtlClntAppOauthSettings) and package.xml
Run sf CLI packaging commands once the human has logged in
Implement PKCE web server flow, instance_url storage and refresh handling
Draft customer-admin install guide (Permitted Users, refresh token policy, permission set)
Draft AppExchange security review docs and run Code Analyzer
human_must: Sign up for DE orgs and verify email
Create the ECA in Setup (or approve CLI deploy) and reveal the consumer secret via email code
Enable Dev Hub and register/link namespace
Accept Salesforce Partner/AppExchange terms and pay review fee
Customer admins: install package and grant access
